documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Here for her yearly visit, turning 42 next month. No complaints. Busy season at work. Denies shortness of breath with stairs, palpitations, ankle swelling or chest discomfort. Taking HCTZ and KCl.

NKDA. Never smoker, no alcohol.
PHQ-2 negative.

Exam: vitals as charted. Well. Neck supple, no JVD. Heart regular, apical low diastolic murmur, no change from prior. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender. Breasts no masses. Legs without edema.

A/P: Healthy visit. Rheumatic mitral disease clinically stable, no symptoms; I brought up cardiology again and she would still like to hold off. CMP, CBC, lipids, A1c today. Screening mammogram ordered. Pap/HPV up to date through 2026. Flu in the fall.

documents.title: Results from your physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Everything came back in the normal range, including potassium and kidney function, cholesterol and your A1c. Please schedule the mammogram at your convenience.

reports.text: Bilateral digital screening mammogram with tomosynthesis, compared with 11/2020. Heterogeneously dense breast tissue. No new mass, distortion or suspicious calcification. Stable appearance bilaterally.

documents.title: Mammogram result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Negative screening mammogram. Normal letter sent.

documents.title: Refill request
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pharmacy e-request: HCTZ 25 mg #90 and KCl ER 20 mEq #90. Labs from March normal. Sent with 3 refills.

documents.title: getting winded
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi doctor, for the last few months I have been getting out of breath going up the stairs at work and even doing laundry and cleaning, and I'm tired all the time. Sometimes my heart flutters. My ankles are puffy at night. No chest pain. Should I come in?

documents.title: RE: getting winded
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Yes, the doctor would like to see you. I booked you for next Tuesday 9/13 at 3:15. If you get short of breath at rest, have chest pain or faint, go to the emergency room or call 911.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit - Dyspnea
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
CC: winded with exertion, tired.

HPI: Over roughly the past several months she has had to stop halfway up the stairs at work and gets breathless with housework, which she never used to. Tired by mid-afternoon. Now and then feels her heart flutter for a few minutes. Ankles swell toward evening and are down by morning. Denies chest pain, cough, or needing to sleep propped up. No fever. Meds unchanged, takes them daily.

Exam: vitals as charted. Comfortable at rest, speaking in full sentences. No JVD. Heart: regular today, loud first sound, low rumbling diastolic murmur at the apex. Lungs clear to auscultation today. Trace to mild ankle edema both sides.

A/P:
1. Exertional dyspnea, fatigue, palpitations and edema in a patient with rheumatic mitral valve disease: concerning for progression of the stenosis. She agrees to cardiology now. Referral placed as urgent; asked them for the earliest new-patient slot. Echo will come through them.
2. Checking CBC, BMP and TSH for other causes of fatigue.
3. Continue HCTZ and KCl, keep salt down. ED precautions reviewed.
Follow up after cardiology.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Your blood count, thyroid and kidney/electrolyte tests are normal, so anemia and thyroid trouble are not the reason for the tiredness. Cardiology has you on October 11 - please keep that appointment.

events.reason: rheumatic mitral valve disease, exertional dyspnea

conditions.label: Rheumatic heart failure
conditions.note: chronic heart failure from mitral stenosis, LVEF 60%

medications.drug: 24 HR metoprolol succinate 50 MG Extended Release Oral Tablet
medications.reason: heart rate control in mitral stenosis

reports.text: Sinus rhythm, rate 92. Normal axis. Normal intervals. No ST-segment or T-wave changes.
reports.conclusion: Sinus rhythm, 92 bpm. No acute ST changes.

reports.text: PA and lateral views. Heart size within normal limits. Mild pulmonary vascular congestion. No pleural effusion, no focal consolidation, no pneumothorax. Bones unremarkable.

Complete 2D, M-mode and Doppler study. Mitral valve: rheumatic appearance with commissural fusion and diastolic doming of the anterior leaflet. Mitral valve area 1.1 cm2 by planimetry. Mean transmitral gradient 10 mmHg at a heart rate of 92. Left atrium enlarged, LA volume index 52 mL/m2. Left ventricle normal in size and wall thickness, LVEF 60%, no regional wall motion abnormality. Right ventricle normal size and function. Estimated PA systolic pressure 38 mmHg. Aortic, tricuspid and pulmonic valves without significant regurgitation or stenosis. No pericardial effusion.
reports.conclusion: Severe rheumatic mitral stenosis (MVA 1.1 cm2, mean gradient 10 mmHg). Enlarged left atrium. Normal LV function, LVEF 60%. Estimated PASP 38 mmHg.

documents.title: Cardiology Consultation
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
Outside cardiology group - consultation letter
Visit date: 10/11/2022
Referred by: primary care
Reason: rheumatic mitral valve disease with worsening exertional symptoms

Thank you for asking us to see this 42-year-old woman. She had rheumatic fever as a child and was told of a mitral valve problem in her teens, but has not been followed by cardiology in many years. Over several months she has become short of breath with stairs and household chores, tires easily, has occasional palpitations and notices her legs swell late in the day. No chest pain, cough or orthopnea.

Medications: hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily, potassium chloride 20 mEq daily.
Allergies: NKDA
PSH: tonsillectomy age 8.
Family: mother with rheumatic fever; father with type 2 diabetes; maternal uncle with stroke at 65.
Social: administrative assistant, never smoker, no alcohol.

Exam: HR 92, BP 118/72. Loud S1. Low-pitched rumbling diastolic murmur at the apex, best with the bell with the patient turned onto her left side. Fine crackles at both bases. Mild ankle edema bilaterally. No JVD.

ECG: sinus rhythm 92, no ST changes.
Chest x-ray: mild pulmonary vascular congestion.
Echo today: rheumatic mitral valve with commissural fusion and doming; MVA 1.1 cm2 by planimetry, mean gradient 10 mmHg at HR 92; LA enlarged (LAVI 52 mL/m2); LVEF 60%; RV normal; PASP estimated 38 mmHg.

Impression:
1. Severe rheumatic mitral stenosis.
2. Chronic heart failure due to mitral stenosis, LV function preserved.
3. Palpitations, rhythm not yet defined.

Plan:
- Start metoprolol succinate 50 mg daily to slow the heart rate and lengthen diastolic filling.
- Continue hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg and KCl 20 mEq; 2 g sodium diet.
- 48-hour Holter to look for atrial fibrillation.
- Return after the Holter.

documents.title: Nurse Visit - Influenza Vaccine
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Flu vaccine 0.5 mL IM left deltoid. Pt mentions she started a new heart pill from cardiology two weeks ago, metoprolol, and is wearing a heart monitor next. Cardiology letter is in the chart. No reactions after waiting.

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet (5 mg) by mouth daily in the evening or as directed by the anticoagulation clinic; goal INR 2.0-3.0
medications.reason: paroxysmal atrial fibrillation with rheumatic mitral stenosis

reports.text: 48-hour ambulatory ECG, 10/18/2022 to 10/20/2022. Predominant rhythm sinus, mean heart rate 88. Three episodes of atrial fibrillation, longest 3 hours 10 minutes; AF burden 6%. Ventricular rate during AF up to 138. Patient-triggered events for palpitations correspond to atrial fibrillation. No pauses, no sustained ventricular arrhythmia.
reports.conclusion: Paroxysmal atrial fibrillation, burden 6%, with symptomatic episodes.

documents.title: Cardiology Follow-up
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
Outside cardiology group - follow-up letter (sent at your request)
Visit date: 11/08/2022

Returns to review her Holter. Tolerating metoprolol, palpitations less frequent. Holter 10/18-10/20: mostly sinus rhythm, mean HR 88, three runs of atrial fibrillation up to 3 h 10 min (burden 6%), rates to 138 in AF, matching her symptom diary.

Impression: paroxysmal atrial fibrillation with severe rheumatic mitral stenosis. Anticoagulation is indicated regardless of risk score in this setting; a DOAC is not appropriate with rheumatic mitral stenosis.

Plan: start warfarin 5 mg daily, dose adjusted to INR 2.0-3.0, managed by our anticoagulation clinic (first INR in one week). Continue metoprolol succinate 50 mg daily, hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg and KCl 20 mEq. Return in 6 months or sooner for symptoms.
Allergies: NKDA.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Back after cardiology. The October consult letter is here (severe rheumatic MS, MVA 1.1 cm2, EF 60%, metoprolol started). She tells me the heart monitor showed atrial fibrillation coming and going and that two weeks ago cardiology started warfarin; their anticoagulation clinic is checking her INR weekly for now. Pharmacy fill history confirms warfarin 5 mg filled 11/8. We do not have that letter or the Holter report yet. Breathing a little better on the metoprolol, still winded on the stairs. Fewer flutters. Ankles less swollen.

Meds now: HCTZ 25 daily, KCl ER 20 mEq daily, metoprolol succinate 50 daily, warfarin 5 mg daily per anticoag clinic.

O: Vitals as charted. Regular rhythm today. Loud S1, apical diastolic rumble. Lungs clear. No edema.

A/P:
1. Severe rheumatic mitral stenosis with chronic heart failure: followed by cardiology. Continue meds and low-salt diet.
2. Paroxysmal AF on warfarin (per patient and pharmacy): will request the cardiology note and Holter. Warfarin teaching: bleeding signs, keep vitamin K foods steady, no ibuprofen or naproxen, acetaminophen is fine, tell us before any new medicine or antibiotic. Warfarin can harm a pregnancy - she is not planning one and understands to tell us right away if that changes.
3. Long-term anticoagulant use added to problem list.
4. BMP and CBC today.
Follow up in 4 months for her physical.

documents.title: Anticoagulation clinic INR log
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Faxed INR flowsheet from the cardiology group's anticoagulation clinic, three point-of-care INRs 11/29 through 12/13 on warfarin 5 mg daily; values entered as results. Clinic moving her to every 2 weeks. Scanned. FYI to PCP.

documents.title: Records request
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Second request to the cardiology office for the 11/8 note and Holter report. They faxed both this morning. Scanned and routed to PCP.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Yearly exam. Says she is about the same as in the fall: OK on flat ground, stops once on the stairs at work. No orthopnea. No bleeding on warfarin, no bruising to speak of. INRs at the cardiology clinic mostly in range, every 2 to 4 weeks now. Palpitations rare.

Meds: HCTZ 25 mg, KCl ER 20 mEq, metoprolol succinate 50 mg, warfarin 5 mg (per anticoag clinic). NKDA.
PHQ-9: 3.

Exam: vitals as charted. Well. No JVD. Regular rhythm, loud S1, apical diastolic rumble. Lungs clear. No edema. Breasts normal. Skin without bruising.

A/P:
1. Severe rheumatic MS, chronic HF, paroxysmal AF on warfarin: stable on current regimen, cardiology recheck due this spring/summer. Holter and November letter reviewed.
2. Pneumococcal vaccine: indicated for her chronic heart disease; PCV20 given today.
3. CMP, CBC, lipids, A1c.
4. Mammogram due next year. Pap/HPV current.
Back in 4 months.

documents.body: Hi Jessenia - your labs look fine. Potassium and kidney function are normal on your water pill and potassium, blood count normal, A1c and cholesterol good.

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Follow-up for valve disease, HF and AF. Feels about the same, heat has made her more tired. Still stops once on the stairs. No orthopnea, no swelling lately, no palpitations in weeks. No bleeding. Has not been back to cardiology since November; says their office will call her.

Meds reviewed, no changes. NKDA.
Exam: vitals as charted. Regular. Loud S1, apical diastolic murmur. Lungs clear. No edema.

A/P: Stable. BMP today for the thiazide/potassium. Asked her to call cardiology to book the 6-month follow-up herself. Flu and COVID vaccines in the fall. Return in 4 to 6 months.

documents.author: RN
documents.body: Influenza vaccine IM left deltoid and 2023-24 COVID vaccine IM right deltoid. On warfarin: fine-gauge needle, firm pressure 2 minutes each site, no hematoma. Observed 15 minutes, no reaction.

documents.title: Telehealth Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video, she is on lunch break at work, identity verified with DOB. Wanted to go over her pills before the holidays and get 90-day supplies. Breathing unchanged from summer: fine walking around the office, short of breath on two flights. No new swelling, no orthopnea. Warfarin managed by the cardiology clinic, last INR she was told was in range. Her cardiology follow-up is booked for April.

Meds: HCTZ 25, KCl ER 20 mEq, metoprolol succinate 50, warfarin per clinic.

Plan: 90-day refills sent for HCTZ, KCl and metoprolol. Warfarin stays with the anticoag clinic. Physical in March with labs and her mammogram.
